readings.section: The Restoration of the Sovereign's Authority
readings.subsection: The Reward of the Faithful Supporter
readings.title: Barzillai Declines the Earthly Court
readings.subtitle: Sustaining the King in Exile Yields Premial Blessing
readings.text:
[2 Samuel 19:31] And Barzillai the Gil‛aḏite came down from Roḡelim and passed over the Yardĕn with the sovereign, to send him on his way over <dn>את</dn> the Yardĕn.
[32] And Barzillai was a very aged man, eighty years old. And he had sustained <dn>את</dn> the sovereign while he was dwelling at Maḥanayim, for he was a very rich man.
[33] And the sovereign said to Barzillai, “Pass over with <dn>את</dn> me, and I shall provide for <dn>את</dn> you with me in Yerushalayim.”
[34] But Barzillai said to the sovereign, “How many are the days of my life, that I should go up with <dn>את</dn> the sovereign to Yerushalayim?
[35] “I am now eighty years old. Do I discern between the good and evil? Does your servant taste <dn>את</dn> what I eat or <dn>את</dn> what I drink? Do I still hear the voice of singing men and singing women? Why then should your servant be a further burden to my master the sovereign?
[36] “Your servant would only pass over <dn>את</dn> the Yardĕn with <dn>את</dn> the sovereign for a short distance. And why should the sovereign repay me with such a reward?
[37] “Please let your servant turn back again to die in my own city, near the burial-site of my father and mother. But here is your servant Kimham, let him pass over with <dn>את</dn> my master the sovereign, and do for him <dn>את</dn> what is good in your eyes.”

readings.section: The Restoration of the Sovereign's Authority
readings.subsection: The Oath to the Next Generation
readings.title: The Sovereign Elevates Kimham
readings.subtitle: Crossing the Boundary of the Jordan
readings.text:
[38] And the sovereign answered, “Kimham is passing over with <dn>את</dn> me, and let me do for him <dn>את</dn> what is good in your eyes. Now whatever you choose of me, I do for you.”
[39] Then all the people went over <dn>את</dn> the Yardĕn. And when the sovereign had passed over, the sovereign kissed Barzillai and blessed him, and he returned to his own place.
[40] And the sovereign passed over to Gilgal, and Kimham passed over with him. And all the people of Yehuḏah brought <dn>את</dn> the sovereign over, and also half the people of Yisra’ĕl.

readings.section: The Restoration of the Sovereign's Authority
readings.title: The Ten Tribes Contend with Yehuḏah
readings.subtitle: Jealousy Ignites the Friction of Division
readings.text:
[2 Samuel 19:41] And see, all the men of Yisra’ĕl were coming to the sovereign! And they said to the sovereign, “Why have our brothers, the men of Yehuḏah, stolen you away and brought <dn>את</dn> the sovereign, and <dn>את</dn> his household, and <dn>את</dn> all Daviḏ’s men with him over <dn>את</dn> the Yardĕn?”
[42] And all the men of Yehuḏah answered the men of Yisra’ĕl, “Because the sovereign is our relative. And why are you displeased over this matter? Have we at all eaten at the sovereign’s cost? Or has he given us any gift?”
[43] And the men of Yisra’ĕl answered <dn>את</dn> the men of Yehuḏah, and said, “We have ten parts in the sovereign, and in Daviḏ too, we have more than you. Why then did you despise us? Was it not our advice first to bring back <dn>את</dn> our sovereign?” But the words of the men of Yehuḏah were harsher than the words of the men of Yisra’ĕl.

readings.title: A Man of Beliya‛al Fractures the Kingdom
readings.subtitle: The Ten Tribes Retreat to Their Tents
readings.text:
[2 Samuel 20:1] And there came to be a man of Beliya‛al, whose name was Sheḇa son of Biḵri, a Binyamite. And he blew with the shophar, and said, “We have no part in Daviḏ, nor do we have inheritance in the son of Yishai – each one to his tents, O Yisra’ĕl!”
[2] Then all the men of Yisra’ĕl deserted Daviḏ, to follow Sheḇa the son of Biḵri. But the men of Yehuḏah, from the Yardĕn as far as Yerushalayim, clung to their sovereign.
[3] And Daviḏ came to his house at Yerushalayim. And the sovereign took <dn>את</dn> the ten women, his concubines whom he had left to look after <dn>את</dn> the house, and put them in a protected house and supported them, but did not go in to them. So they were shut up to the day of their death, living in widowhood.

readings.subsection: The Attrition of the King's Command
readings.title: Yo’aḇ’s Ruthless Execution of Amasa
readings.subtitle: Political Assassination on the Highway
readings.text:
[4] And the sovereign said to Amasa, “Call <dn>את</dn> the men of Yehuḏah for me within three days, and be present here yourself.”
[5] And Amasa went to call <dn>את</dn> the men of Yehuḏah. But he delayed longer than <dn>את</dn> the appointed time which Daviḏ had appointed him.
[6] And Daviḏ said to Aḇishai, “Now Sheḇa son of Biḵri is going to do us more evil than Aḇshalom. Take <dn>את</dn> the servants of your master, and pursue him, lest he find for himself walled cities, and escape us.”
[7] Then the men of Yo’aḇ went out after him, with the Kerĕthites and the Pelĕthites, and all the mighty men. And they went out of Yerushalayim to pursue Sheḇa son of Biḵri.
[8] When they were near the large stone which is in Giḇ’on, Amasa came before them. And Yo’aḇ was dressed in battle armour, and on it was a girdle with a sword fastened in its sheath at his hips. And as he went forward, it fell out.
[9] And Yo’aḇ said to Amasa, “Peace, my brother?” And Yo’aḇ took Amasa by the beard with his right hand to kiss him.
[10] But Amasa was not on guard against the sword in Yo’aḇ’s hand. And he struck him with it in the stomach, and his inward parts poured out on the ground, and he did not strike him again, and he died. Then Yo’aḇ and Aḇishai his brother pursued Sheḇa son of Biḵri.
[11] And a man, one of Yo’aḇ’s men, stood beside him, and said, “Whoever is well pleased with Yo’aḇ and whoever is for Daviḏ, let him follow Yo’aḇ!”
[12] And Amasa was rolling in his blood in the middle of the highway. And the man saw that all the people stood still, so he moved <dn>את</dn> Amasa from the highway to the field and threw a garment over him, when he saw that everyone who came upon him halted.
[13] When he was removed from the highway, all the men passed on after Yo’aḇ to pursue Sheḇa son of Biḵri.

readings.title: A Wise Woman Negotiates for the City
readings.subtitle: The Adversary's Head Thrown Over the Wall
readings.text:
[2 Samuel 20:14] And he passed over through all the tribes of Yisra’ĕl to Aḇĕl, and to Bĕyth Ma‛aḵah, and to all the Bĕrites. And they were assembled and went after him too.
[15] And they went and besieged him in Aḇĕl of Bĕyth Ma‛aḵah, and they cast up a siege mound against the city. And it stood in a rampart, and all the people who were with <dn>את</dn> Yo’aḇ battered the wall to throw it down.
[16] Then a wise woman called out from the city, “Listen, listen! Please say to Yo’aḇ, ‘Come nearby, so that I speak to you.’ ”
[17] And he came near to her, and the woman said, “Are you Yo’aḇ?” And he answered, “I am.” Then she said to him, “Listen to the words of your female servant.” And he answered, “I am listening.”
[18] Then she spoke, saying, “In former times they often spoke, saying, ‘Let them inquire of Aḇĕl,’ and so they ended the matter.
[19] “I am of the peaceable and trustworthy ones in Yisra’ĕl. You seek to destroy a city and a mother in Yisra’ĕl. Why do you swallow up <dn>את</dn> the inheritance of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>?”
[20] And Yo’aḇ answered and said, “Far be it, far be it from me to swallow up or to destroy!
[21] “That is not the case. But a man from the mountains of Ephrayim, Sheḇa son of Biḵri by name, has raised <dn>את</dn> his hand against the sovereign, against Daviḏ. Hand him over, him alone, and I withdraw from the city.” And the woman said to Yo’aḇ, “Look, his head is going to be thrown to you over the wall.”
[22] So the woman in her wisdom went to all the people. And they cut off <dn>את</dn> the head of Sheḇa son of Biḵri, and threw it out to Yo’aḇ. Then he blew with the shophar, and they dispersed from the city, each one to his tent. And Yo’aḇ returned to the sovereign at Yerushalayim.

readings.title: The Administrators of Yisra’ĕl
readings.subtitle: Establishing Order After the Breach
readings.text:
[23] Now Yo’aḇ was over all the army of Yisra’ĕl, and Benayah son of Yehoyaḏa was over the Kerĕthites and the Pelĕthites,
[24] and Aḏoram was over the compulsory labour, and Yehoshaphat son of Aḥiluḏ was recorder,
[25] and Sheva was scribe, and Tsaḏoq and Eḇyathar were the priests,
[26] and Ira the Ya‛irite was priest to Daviḏ.

readings.title: YeHoVaH Answers the Scarcity
readings.subtitle: The Debt of Sha’ul’s Broken Oath
readings.text:
[2 Samuel 21:1] And there was a scarcity of food in the days of Daviḏ for three years, year after year. And Daviḏ sought <dn>את</dn> the face of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> answered, <dq>“Because of Sha’ul and his bloodthirsty house, because he killed <dn>את</dn> the Giḇ’onites.”</dq>
[2] The sovereign therefore called the Giḇ’onites and spoke to them. Now the Giḇ’onites were not of the children of Yisra’ĕl, but of the remnant of the Amorites. And the children of Yisra’ĕl had sworn protection to them, but Sha’ul had sought to strike them in his ardour for the children of Yisra’ĕl and Yehuḏah.
[3] So Daviḏ said to the Giḇ’onites, “What should I do for you? And with what do I make atonement, so that you bless <dn>את</dn> the inheritance of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>?”
[4] And the Giḇ’onites said to him, “It is no matter of silver or gold between us and Sha’ul, or his house, neither is it for us to put to death any man in Yisra’ĕl.” And he said, “Whatever you say I do for you.”
[5] And they said to the sovereign, “The man who consumed us and plotted against us, that we should be destroyed from remaining in all the border of Yisra’ĕl,
[6] let seven men of his sons be given to us, and we shall hang them before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> in Giḇ‛ah of Sha’ul, whom <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> chose.” And the sovereign said, “I give them.”

readings.title: The Covenant with Yehonathan Honored
readings.subtitle: A Harvest of Retributive Justice
readings.text:
[7] But the sovereign spared Mephiḇosheth son of Yehonathan, son of Sha’ul, because of the oath of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> that was between them, between Daviḏ and Yehonathan son of Sha’ul.
[8] And the sovereign took <dn>את</dn> the two sons of Ritspah the daughter of Ayah, whom she bore to Sha’ul: <dn>את</dn> Armoni and <dn>את</dn> the other Mephiḇosheth, and <dn>את</dn> the five sons of Miḵal the daughter of Sha’ul, whom she brought up for Aḏri’ĕl the son of Barzillai, the Meḥolathite,
[9] and gave them into the hands of the Giḇ’onites, and they hanged them on the hill before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. So the seven fell together, and were put to death in the days of harvest, in the first days, in the beginning of barley harvest.

readings.title: Ritspah Guards the Exposed Bodies
readings.subtitle: The Land Receives the Atonement
readings.text:
[10] And Ritspah the daughter of Ayah took <dn>את</dn> sackcloth and spread it for herself on the rock, from the beginning of harvest until the late rains poured on them from the heavens. And she did not allow the birds of the heavens to rest on them by day nor <dn>את</dn> the beasts of the field by night.
[11] And Daviḏ was informed <dn>את</dn> what Ritspah the daughter of Ayah, the concubine of Sha’ul, had done.
[12] And Daviḏ went and took <dn>את</dn> the bones of Sha’ul, and <dn>את</dn> the bones of Yehonathan his son, from the men of Yaḇĕsh Gil‛aḏ who had stolen them from the street of Bĕyth Shan, where the Philistines had hung them up, after the Philistines had struck down <dn>את</dn> Sha’ul in Gilboa.
[13] And he brought up the bones of Sha’ul and <dn>את</dn> the bones of Yehonathan his son from there, and they gathered <dn>את</dn> the bones of those who had been hanged,
[14] and buried <dn>את</dn> the bones of Sha’ul and <dn>את</dn> Yehonathan his son in the land of Binyamin in Tsela, in the burial-site of Qish his father, and did all that the sovereign commanded. And after that <dn>Elohim</dn> heard prayer for the land.

readings.title: The Extinction of the Philistine Giants
readings.subtitle: The Sovereign's Men Extinguish the Genetic Threat
readings.text:
[2 Samuel 21:15] And the Philistines were again fighting against Yisra’ĕl, so Daviḏ and his servants with <dn>את</dn> him went down and fought against the Philistines. And Daviḏ was weary,
[16] and Yishbo-Benoḇ – who was one of the sons of the giant, the weight of whose bronze spear was three hundred pieces, who was bearing a new sword – spoke of striking <dn>את</dn> Daviḏ.
[17] But Aḇishai son of Tseruyah came to help him, and struck <dn>את</dn> the Philistine and killed him. Then Daviḏ’s men swore to him, saying, “Do not go out with <dn>את</dn> us to battle any more, lest you put out <dn>את</dn> the lamp of Yisra’ĕl.”
[18] And it came to be afterward, that there was a battle again with the Philistines at Goḇ. Then Sibbeḵai the Ḥushathite struck <dn>את</dn> Saph, who was one of the sons of the giant.
[19] And there was a battle with the Philistines again at Goḇ, where Elḥanan son of Ya‛arĕy-Oreḡim the Bĕyth Leḥemite struck <dn>את</dn> Golyath the Gittite, the shaft of whose spear was like a weaver’s beam.
[20] And there was a battle in Gath again, where there was a man of great height, who had six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot, twenty-four in number. And he also was descended from the giants.
[21] And he reproached <dn>את</dn> Yisra’ĕl, and Yehonathan son of Shim‛i, the brother of Daviḏ, struck him.
[22] These four were born to the giant in Gath, and they fell by the hand of Daviḏ and by the hand of his servants.

readings.subsection: The Chronological Record of the Wars
readings.title: Striking Down the Giants of Gath
readings.subtitle: The Parallel Testimony of Victory
readings.text:
[1 Chronicles 20:4] And afterward it came to be that fighting broke out at Gezer with the Philistines. Then Sibbeḵai the Ḥushathite struck <dn>את</dn> Sippai of the sons of the giant, and they were humbled.
[5] And there was fighting again with the Philistines, and Elḥanan son of Ya’ir struck <dn>את</dn> Laḥmi the brother of Golyath the Gittite, the shaft of whose spear was like a weaver’s beam.
[6] And there was fighting again at Gath, where there was a man of great size, with twenty-four fingers and toes, six and six. And he too was born to the giant.
[7] And he reproached <dn>את</dn> Yisra’ĕl, and Yehonathan son of Shim‛a, Daviḏ’s brother, struck him.
[8] These were born to the giant in Gath, and they fell by the hand of Daviḏ and by the hand of his servants.

readings.title: Refuge in the Face of the Lion
readings.subtitle: A Shiggaion Against Unrighteous Hands
readings.text:
[Psalm 7:1] O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> my <dn>Elohim</dn>, in <dn>You</dn> I have taken refuge; Save me from all my pursuers; And deliver me,
[2] Lest they tear at my throat like a lion, Rending in pieces, with no one to deliver.
[3] O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> my <dn>Elohim</dn>, if I have done this: If there is unrighteousness in my hands,
[4] If I have done evil to him who was at peace with me, Or have plundered my enemy without cause,
[5] Let the enemy pursue me and overtake my being, And trample my life to the ground, And lay my esteem in the dust. Selah.

readings.subsection: The Court of the Most High
readings.title: YeHoVaH Commands the Judgment
readings.subtitle: The Trier of Hearts and Kidneys Takes the Bench
readings.text:
[6] Arise, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, in <dn>Your</dn> displeasure; Lift <dn>Yourself</dn> up against the rage of my adversaries, And awake for me! <dn>You</dn> shall command judgment!
[7] And let the congregation of the peoples gather about <dn>You</dn>; And over them return on high.
[8] <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> judges the peoples; Judge me, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, according to my righteousness, And according to my integrity within me.
[9] Please let the evil of the wrong be ended, And establish the righteous; For the righteous <dn>Elohim</dn> is a trier of hearts and kidneys.

readings.title: Elohim Sharpens His Sword
readings.subtitle: The Unerring Accuracy of Divine Retribution
readings.text:
[Psalm 7:10] My shield is upon <dn>Elohim</dn>, <dn>Who</dn> saves the upright in heart.
[11] <dn>Elohim</dn> is a righteous judge. And <dn>Ĕl</dn> is enraged every day,
[12] If one does not repent! <dn>He</dn> sharpens <dn>His</dn> sword, <dn>He</dn> bends <dn>His</dn> bow and makes it ready,
[13] And <dn>He</dn> has prepared for <dn>Himself</dn> instruments of death, <dn>He</dn> makes <dn>His</dn> arrows hot for pursuers.

readings.title: The Pitfall of the Adversary
readings.subtitle: Trouble Turns Back Upon the Head of the Wicked
readings.text:
[14] See, he who is bound with wickedness, And has conceived trouble and brought forth falsehood,
[15] He has made a pit and dug it out, And falls into the ditch he made!
[16] His trouble turns back upon his own head, And his wrongdoing comes down on the top of his head.
[17] I give thanks to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> according to <dn>His</dn> righteousness, And praise the Name of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> Most High.
